technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) module conventions and supported Spring Framework 6 / Java 17 baseline.
Preserve the externally visible behavior and configuration properties of the corresponding Spring XD modules unless an adaptation is required by the s-c-s programming model.
Implement mqtt, null, shell, splunk, and tcp as sink modules; implement jdbc as a source module; and implement aggregator and http-client as processor modules.
Reuse existing Spring Integration, Spring Cloud Stream binder, and protocol/client libraries where compatible rather than introducing custom transport abstractions.
Expose module configuration through the repository's standard configuration metadata and naming conventions.
Prefer focused unit tests with mocked external systems, supplemented by targeted integration tests for JDBC, MQTT, TCP, Splunk, and HTTP behavior.
Treat the aggregator as a stateful processor and retain its correlation, release, and message-group semantics while adapting lifecycle and message-channel integration to s-c-s.
Use the repository's existing build, formatting, static-analysis, packaging, and continuous-integration conventions.
assumptions: The target s-c-s repository and the source Spring XD module implementations are available, buildable, and licensed for reuse.
The increment covers implementation, adaptation, tests, documentation, and CI integration, but not production deployment or operational rollout.
No major redesign of module behavior, public APIs, or protocol semantics is required beyond migration from Spring XD to s-c-s.
Existing repository infrastructure, parent build files, dependency management, and module templates can be reused with limited modification.

External systems such as brokers, databases, Splunk, TCP endpoints, shells, and HTTP services can be represented by local test doubles or containerized test services; provisioning shared environments is out of scope.
Backward compatibility is required for the principal module options and message behavior, but exact Spring XD command-line packaging compatibility is not required.
One developer performs all analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, code review preparation, and integration work sequentially.
Effort is expressed in workdays and excludes elapsed waiting time for external reviews, infrastructure access, or release approvals.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the Spring XD implementations, existing s-c-s module patterns, supported dependency versions, configuration properties, message contracts, and migration risks; produce the implementation plan and module mapping.

activities.activity_name: Repository scaffolding and shared build integration
activities.activity_description: Create or adapt module directories, Gradle or Maven configuration, dependency management, packaging conventions, configuration metadata, common test infrastructure, and local build execution for the migrated modules.
Adapt the MQTT sink implementation to the s-c-s module contract, configure MQTT client and message conversion behavior, preserve relevant options, and add focused unit tests.
Implement the no-op/null sink using the s-c-s sink contract, preserve expected discard behavior and configuration, and add unit tests.
Adapt process execution, input streaming, exit/error handling, configuration, and lifecycle behavior for the shell sink, with tests using controlled local commands.
Adapt Splunk event submission, endpoint and authentication configuration, payload conversion, error handling, and test coverage using mocked or local HTTP interactions.
Adapt TCP connection management, payload encoding, reconnect/error behavior, configuration, and tests using a controllable TCP test server.
Adapt polling or query execution, row-to-message conversion, scheduling, database configuration, transaction/error behavior, and tests against an embedded or containerized database.

Port stateful message grouping, correlation, release strategy, timeout, persistence or lifecycle behavior as applicable, adapt it to the s-c-s processor contract, and implement comprehensive unit tests.
Adapt outbound HTTP request construction, response mapping, headers, timeouts, error handling, configuration, and processor channel behavior, with tests against a stub HTTP service.

Run the complete build and test matrix, validate source-to-processor-to-sink pipeline wiring, verify configuration metadata and packaging, test supported Java and dependency compatibility, and fix integration defects.
Document module purpose, configuration properties, input/output contracts, required external services, representative streaming pipeline examples, and migration notes from Spring XD.
